sentences.text:
The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No.1943 of 2016, under sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120B I.P.C., 1860 and Section 13(1)(c), 13(2) and 8 of Prevention of Corruption Act, Police Station Vijay Nagar, District Ghaziabad,
with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.
3.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits, FIR of the present case was lodged in the year 2016 against applicant and others and, as per allegation, applicant was posted as Chief Manager in the bank and he alongwith other accused persons, fraudulently disbursed loan of Rs.55 lakhs in favour of co-accused Satya Deo Singh, but the entire allegations made against applicant are totally false and baseless.
He further submits, after following due process, the loan was disbursed in favour of the co-accused Satya Deo Singh.
He further submits, the co-accused Satya Deo Singh has already been released on bail.
4. He further submits, however, FIR of the present case was lodged in the year 2016, but in April,
2025 police started making attempt to arrest him.
He further submits, after 9 years from the date of FIR, there is no need to send the applicant behind bars.
He further submits, applicant has already retired from service in the year 2016.

5. He further submits, apart from the present case, applicant has criminal history of two other cases,
but in one case, after investigation final report has been submitted and in one another case, he is on bail.
He further submits, applicant is having apprehension, if he will appear before the court concerned then he will be sent to jail.
6. He further submits, therefore, applicant should be enlarged on anticipatory bail till the conclusion of the trial.

7. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
8.
I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

sentences.text:
However, as per allegation, applicant, who was the Chief Manager of the bank alongwith others,
fraudulently and illegally disbursed the loan of Rs.55 lakhs in favour of co-accused Satya Deo Singh but it reflects that FIR of the present case was lodged in the year 2016 and
till then with regard to applicant, the investigation is still pending.10.

Further, however it reflects that the name of the applicant has been surfaced during investigation but thereafter Investigating Officer did not propose to arrest the applicant and it appears that after several years he started making attempt of his arrest.

11. The Apex Court in the case of Gursewak Singh Vs. State of Punjab (Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.)
No.11234 of 2025 dated 3.9.2025 observed that as after four years from the FIR Investigating Officer tried to arrest the accused, therefore, this itself was a good ground to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

entities.text:

No.11234 of 2025
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. Further, the applicant had already retired from service in the year 2016, and considering the facts of the case, in the considered view of this court, after 9 years from the date of FIR, it is not proper to send the applicant behind bars.
13. Further, apprehension of arrest raised by applicant cannot be completely ruled out.

Further,
apart from the present case, applicant has criminal history of two other cases, but in one case, after investigation final report has been submitted and in one another case, he is on bail.
14.
Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial.
15. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant anticipatory bail application is allowed.

sentences.text: In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.

18. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

(Sameer Jain,J.) November 7, 2025 Anurag/-
